Douglas P. Marsh

Green candidate for U.S. Senate, Michigan · Open seat

Journalist

Douglas P. Marsh is the Green Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan in the November 3, 2026 general election, running for the open seat left by Sen. Gary Peters (D), who is not seeking re-election. He was also the Green Party's U.S. Senate nominee in Michigan in 2024. He finished third of six candidates that year with 53,978 votes (0.97%). He was born in Traverse City and describes himself as a community journalist.

Where Marsh stands

Foreign policy / Iran
Opposes more spending on wars abroad and on weapons. Argues the money could go to domestic programs instead. Lists a ceasefire among his priorities.
Economy and cost of living
Lists affordability and changes to the housing market among his campaign priorities.
Health care
Supports universal health care, which he lists as one of his priorities.
Environment / water
Lists clean water among his campaign priorities.

Background

  • Green Party nominee, U.S. Senate, Michigan, 2026
  • Green Party nominee, U.S. Senate, Michigan, 2024 (lost; 0.97%)
  • Occupation: journalist; past jobs include educator, firefighter, landscaper, ski patroller and coal passer
  • Education: B.A. in philosophy, University of Michigan, 2006
